geometry.note: This way has only 3 nodes and traces roughly 1.28 km; the historic Canfranc railway tunnel is commonly cited at about 7.8 km, so this is a partial trace of one portal area only, not the whole tunnel. No other OSM way for the rest of the tunnel was found this session (Nominatim name searches for 'Pau-Canfranc tunnel' and 'Somport railway tunnel' both returned zero results, and Overpass — which could have found it by bbox or relation membership — was unreachable throughout). Drawn as-is rather than omitted, clearly labelled as partial.

method: OpenStreetMap way 1081204524 taken verbatim (its full, and only, 3 nodes). No lengthening or extrapolation attempted.
name: Túnel ferroviario de Somport (historic rail tunnel, partial trace)
notes: LSC's own history describes its halls as excavated between this historic (1928) single-track railway tunnel and the newer (2003) road tunnel (src:lsc-history); this record draws only the ~1.28 km fraction of the rail tunnel that OpenStreetMap happens to trace near one portal, honestly flagged as partial rather than extended by guesswork.

summary.plain: A short, partially-mapped stretch of the historic (1928) Canfranc railway tunnel, near one of its portals; OpenStreetMap does not yet trace the tunnel's full length.
